document: Alone Against The Frost Solitaire Adventure in Canadas Wilds (Glenn Rahman  Gavin Inglis) (z-library.sk, 1lib.sk, z-lib.sk).pdf

paragraphs.text:
If you let Bernard run, you may lose him forever in the dark 
maze  of  trees  and  sloughs.  You  dash  after  him,  yelling  his 
name. Ahead you hear running steps, snapping brittle brush 
and frosted grass. You cannot explain this unseasonable cold 
snap, but you can spare no time to think on it.

Now, you hear a second runner join the first. The ground 
shudders  with  footfalls  that  could  come  from  no  creature 
smaller than a moose. Abruptly, the sounds of running cease. 
Under faint moonlight, you break into an empty clearing.

A piteous cry rings forth from the sky overhead: “Oh! The 
height! My feet! My burning feet!”

To look up toward the shout, go to 72. To cover your ears, shut your 
eyes, and wait until the plaintive appeal is gone, attempt a POW 
roll; if you succeed, go to 49; if you fail, go to 48.
